questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the central idea of “Container Security Fundamentals”?
options: Reduce privileges and network/mount exposure while testing the application’s actual requirements.
Run every application as root and in privileged mode for compatibility.
Put secrets in Dockerfile ARG or ENV values so they are easy to inspect.
Expose the Docker daemon without authentication to simplify remote management.
questions.answer_key: Reduce privileges and network/mount exposure while testing the application’s actual requirements.
questions.explanation: Non-root execution, capability reduction, secure daemon access and secret-safe builds are important defense-in-depth controls.

questions.prompt: For a lab covering container security fundamentals, what is the strongest evidence of learning?
options: Assume the command is portable and skip reading its output.
Make several unrelated changes before collecting a baseline.
Use a production host so the result looks realistic.
Record the command or configuration, predicted result, observed evidence, and one relevant edge case.
questions.answer_key: Record the command or configuration, predicted result, observed evidence, and one relevant edge case.
questions.explanation: A useful lab connects a predicted result to actual output and checks an edge case. This is safer and more reproducible than assuming success.

questions.prompt: If an example related to container security fundamentals fails, which response is best?
options: Disable permissions or security controls until the example works.
Trust the image tag without inspecting the image or version.
Reproduce the issue, inspect state/logs/configuration, test one hypothesis at a time, and verify the fix.
Delete every stopped container and unused volume before investigating.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the issue, inspect state/logs/configuration, test one hypothesis at a time, and verify the fix.
questions.explanation: The evidence-led approach keeps the diagnosis reproducible and avoids hiding the cause. For container security fundamentals, verify the fix with the exact setting or command that failed.
